title: Invoices, bills, credit notes & payments
summary: Customer invoices from sales orders, vendor bills from purchase orders, manual invoices/bills, posting with numbering and due dates from payment terms, taxes, credit notes, payment registration with partial payments.
design: Odoo-inspired, Mendix-native (intake Q3): Odoo is the functional reference; simplifications listed and signed off at the Stage 2 gate

useCases.title: Invoice sales orders
postconditions: Draft customer invoice(s) with lines for the quantities to invoice
mainFlow: 1. User clicks Create invoice on an order (or selects several in the To invoice list)
2. System creates one draft invoice per customer (optionally consolidated) with a line per order line to invoice, plus sections/notes
3. Copies payment term, salesperson, references; links order lines
4. Order invoice status recomputed

useCases.title: Create a vendor bill from a purchase order
postconditions: Draft vendor bill linked to the PO
mainFlow: 1. User clicks Create bill on the PO
2. System creates a draft bill with lines for the quantities to bill (ordered or received per bill policy)
3. User enters the vendor bill reference and bill date

useCases.title: Create a manual invoice or bill
mainFlow: 1. User opens Customers > Invoices (or Vendors > Bills) > New
2. Enters partner, dates, lines (product, qty, price, taxes)
3. System recomputes totals and due date

useCases.title: Post an invoice
preconditions: Draft with at least one line, partner and (for bills) bill date
postconditions: Posted, numbered, due date set, amount due = total; order invoiced quantities updated
mainFlow: 1. User clicks Confirm
2. System validates (partner, lines, positive total; bill date for vendor bills)
3. Sets invoice date = today if empty; due date from payment term
4. Assigns the number (INV/BILL/RINV/RBILL + year)
5. Status Posted, payment status NotPaid; updates sales/purchase invoiced quantities

useCases.title: Reset to draft or cancel
mainFlow: 1. Reset to draft: Posted -> Draft (number kept)
2. Cancel: Draft -> Cancelled

useCases.title: Issue a credit note
postconditions: Credit note linked to the original; optionally reconciled
mainFlow: 1. User clicks Credit note and enters reason and date
2. System creates a draft credit note (CustomerCreditNote/VendorCreditNote) copying the lines
3. Posting the credit note reduces the amount due of the original (allocation), marking it Reversed when fully offset

useCases.title: Register a payment
postconditions: Payment Paid; invoices PartiallyPaid/Paid; amount due reduced
mainFlow: 1. User clicks Register payment on one or more invoices of one partner
2. System proposes amount = total due, date = today, method Bank transfer
3. User may lower the amount (partial payment) and sets memo
4. System creates the payment with allocations to invoices (oldest due first) and recomputes payment status

useCases.title: Follow up receivables and payables
mainFlow: 1. User filters invoices on payment status and overdue (due date < today)
2. Opens Reporting > Invoices for totals per partner/period

useCases.title: Maintain taxes and payment terms
postconditions: Taxes/terms usable on products, partners and documents
mainFlow: 1. Manager maintains taxes (name, scope, percentage/fixed, amount, included in price)
2. Maintains payment terms with instalment lines

simplifications: No general ledger: no chart of accounts, journal items for receivable/payable/tax, journals, reconciliation or bank statements.
account.move restricted to invoices, bills and credit notes; journal sequences replaced by Core.Sequence per invoice type.
Payments allocated to invoices through Invoicing.PaymentAllocation instead of reconciliation of journal items.
Taxes: percentage or fixed, included or excluded; no groups, repartition, fiscal positions, cash basis.
Down payments, early-payment discounts, cash rounding, EDI/e-invoicing and sending by email dropped.

no ledger: sales/purchase journals become invoice types, bank/cash journals become ENUM_PaymentMethod
tax groups (subtotal grouping) — dropped; taxes summed per tax
tax repartition to accounts — no ledger
